resources.string: Colloid-facing edge of one follicular cell wedge
Outer edge of one wedge: %1$s u
Inner edge = 2 × π × lumen radius ÷ number of wedges. Outer edge = 2 × π × (lumen radius + 2 u) ÷ number of wedges. The chart rounds the wedge count to a whole number.

Thyroid follicular cells line a cavity called the lumen. Their inner (apical) face borders the colloid, which stores thyroglobulin. Their outer (basal) face points toward tissue and nearby capillaries. Picture a slice with colloid in the center and equal cell wedges forming a ring 2 u thick. The two edge lengths are arcs in that slice, not surface areas. The circle, wedge counts and lengths are invented; u is an arbitrary drawing unit, not a measurement or a predictor of hormone output.
